summary: Palden Sherab (1938–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gochen Monastery and Riwoche Monastery (~1953–1959) under Dudjom Rinpoche, Tubten Tsondru, and others. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at CIHTS (~1967–1984).

Palmira Brummett is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She served at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and as visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a Tibetology scholar. She studied under Per Kværne (attested 2012), Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held posts at Temple University (attested 2001) and Elon University, where she was Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University (~1972–1976).

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. His posts included teaching at Elphinstone College (1909), Government Law College (~1917–1923), and serving as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

Paolo Visigalli is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Padua, and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at NYU Shanghai (~2017–2021) and Shanghai Normal University (~2021).

Paride Stortini specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied as a doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026) and was appointed as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Parimal G. Patil is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002). He has served as a professor at Harvard University (~2001).

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pascale Haag is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay, holding a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~2003).
Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).
Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. She served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum and as professor at UC Berkeley (1996).

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister is a Japanology and art history scholar who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas. She held positions at the University of Kansas, Hakuho Women's College, and served as professor at Nichibunken (2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and IKGA (~2012).

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).
